programme.title: ...Sings Dylan II
programme.desc: A feast of cover versions of Bob Dylan songs from the BBC archives, with classic tracks old and new and some surprises from the 1960s to the present. From the essential folk queen Joan Baez to punk princess Siouxsie and the Banshees, from The Hollies to Adele, taking in the likes of Julie Felix, Richie Havens, Bryan Ferry and KT Tunstall along the way, the programme reflects Dylan's long career of writing extraordinary songs and the fascination of other artists with them. Peter, Paul and Mary's sublime The Times They Are A-Changin' rubs shoulders with the close harmony of Cliff Richard and The Nolan Sisters' smooth interpretation of the protest classic Blowin' in the Wind. The Blues Band's energetic 1980s updating of Maggie's Farm contrasts with Tom Jones's powerful rootsy What Good Am I? A treat for the Dylan fan and the Dylan novice alike.

programme.title: My Favourite Cake
programme.desc: One night. Two lonely hearts. Endless possibilities. Seventy-year-old Mahin lives alone in Tehran since her husband's death and her daughter's departure for Europe, until an afternoon tea with friends leads her to break her solitary routine and revitalise her love life. But as Mahin opens herself up to romance, what begins as an unexpected encounter quickly evolves into an unpredictable, unforgettable evening. The film explores themes of love, regret and second chances. It’s set against the backdrop of a country with strict rules and restrictions, especially when it comes to the rights and freedoms of women. In Farsi with English subtitles.

programme.title: King Otto and Football’s Greek Gods
programme.desc: In the summer of 2004, audiences looked on in disbelief as the Greek national football team, who had never previously won a single match or even scored a goal in a major tournament, took down the giants of world football to become the unlikeliest of European champions. The architect behind this unprecedented triumph was legendary German football coach ‘King’ Otto Rehhagel. After accomplishing every major success in Germany, he made the bold decision to leave all he knew behind and work in a foreign country with the underachieving Greek national team. This is the story of how these two contrasting cultures came together to speak the same language and write a new chapter of Greek mythology.

programme.desc: In the summer of 2004, audiences looked on in disbelief as the Greek national football team, who had never previously won a single match or even scored a goal in a major tournament, took down the giants of world football to become the unlikeliest of European champions. The architect behind this unprecedented triumph was legendary German football coach ‘King’ Otto Rehhagel. After accomplishing every major success in Germany, he made the bold decision to leave all he knew behind and work in a foreign country with the underachieving Greek national team. This is the story of how these two contrasting cultures came together to speak the same language and write a new chapter of Greek mythology.

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: Hyacinth finds herself with an ideal opportunity to impress Emmet with her singing when she discovers that he is involved in a concert at the church hall. However, Richard has other things on his mind, dreading the thought of early retirement and having to spend more time with his wife.

programme.title: Sorry!
programme.desc: Timothy, after some initial complications, is asked to be best man at his friend Frank's wedding. He ends up in trouble as a result of trying to encourage the idea of marriage in spite of his parents.

programme.title: The Good Old Days
programme.desc: Leonard Sachs presents an edition of the old time music hall programme, first broadcast on 24 February 1977. With Larry Grayson, Fenella Fielding, Hinge and Bracket, Anna Sharkey and members of the Players' Theatre, London.

programme.title: Tech Now
programme.desc: Shiona McCallum meets the medical expert testing out the future of prosthetics following his own near-fatal cycling accident. Paul Carter heads inside Amazon's AI chip lab in Austin, Texas. Zoe Kleinman visits the UK Dementia Research Institute to see how AI is being used to improve diagnosis and help find treatments. Harriet Bradshaw finds out how gym equipment is being invented and tested to help astronauts exercise in space.

programme.title: Rachel Khoo's Kitchen Notebook
programme.desc: Rachel indulges her passion for the Swedish outdoors, inspired by both the woodland and the water. Whilst visiting the Swedish Archipelago, Rachel shows off her fishing skills and gets into the Scandinavian way of life cooking a perch-style wrap on an open fire at the waterside by a traditional Swedish cabin. Back home, Rachel recreates Swedish favourites with her very own Khoo twist. She makes a savoury Swedish celebration cake, known as smörgåstårta, a wild mushroom soup with dill fish balls and an edible forest floor.

programme.title: The Travel Show
programme.desc: It's an important year for the city of Hull, in northern England. It's celebrating more than 800 years of maritime history with a raft of new museum openings that it's hoped will make it a world-class visitor attraction. Emeline Nsingi Nkosi goes to see the opening of the restored Spurn Lightship - literally a lighthouse on a ship - which was a mainstay on the waterways there for 50 years. She meets the people involved in the huge regeneration effort and finds out why the city's been the punchline of jokes for so many years.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Helen and Kevin are nearing full retirement and have a garden dominated by three things – a patio that looks too big for the space, a breeze-block wall that looks ugly and a shed that sticks out like a sore thumb. Inspired by Portugal's granite stone sets and raised boardwalks, they like the idea of a low-maintenance seaside garden with little or no lawn and drought-resistant plants like thistles and grasses. With a budget of £4,000, Charlie and Lee have a challenge ahead to craft this coastal oasis despite being 100 miles from the sea.

programme.title: Shrek
programme.desc: Animated comedy. In a land of living fairy tales and nursery rhymes, grumpy ogre Shrek, along with the loudmouthed Donkey, joins beautiful but wilful Princess Fiona in tackling Lord Farquaad's evil schemes to exile the exotic from his lands and wed the unwilling princess.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents this high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team featuring rugby player and podcaster Joe Marler, actor Jennie McAlpine, comedian Geoff Norcott and presenter Jean Johannson as they take on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: They say don't walk under a ladder... Jacqui does more than that, and designer Ayo unlocks the potential of a £2 table with a bold design.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Helen and Kevin are nearing full retirement and have a garden dominated by three things – a patio that looks too big for the space, a breeze-block wall that looks ugly and a shed that sticks out like a sore thumb. Inspired by Portugal's granite stone sets and raised boardwalks, they like the idea of a low-maintenance seaside garden with little or no lawn and drought-resistant plants like thistles and grasses. With a budget of £4,000, Charlie and Lee have a challenge ahead to craft this coastal oasis despite being 100 miles from the sea.

programme.title: Shrek
programme.desc: Animated comedy. In a land of living fairy tales and nursery rhymes, grumpy ogre Shrek, along with the loudmouthed Donkey, joins beautiful but wilful Princess Fiona in tackling Lord Farquaad's evil schemes to exile the exotic from his lands and wed the unwilling princess.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents this high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team featuring rugby player and podcaster Joe Marler, actor Jennie McAlpine, comedian Geoff Norcott and presenter Jean Johannson as they take on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Two Weeks in August

Solomon is the only one who doesn’t know what happened last night - does Zoe tell him and destroy two marriages? Jess is forced to take drastic action to avoid confrontation.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies

One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Two Weeks in August

programme.title: Bridge of Lies

programme.title: Shrek
programme.desc: Animated comedy. In a land of living fairy tales and nursery rhymes, grumpy ogre Shrek, along with the loudmouthed Donkey, joins beautiful but wilful Princess Fiona in tackling Lord Farquaad's evil schemes to exile the exotic from his lands and wed the unwilling princess.

programme.title: 21st Century TV with Lucy Owen
programme.desc: BBC Wales’s Lucy Owen looks back at 2006 and the New Year tradition of waterfall karate. The Welsh contestants on Big Brother cause a stir, and Cardiff Library packs up and moves. There’s a jazzy celebration on the 250th anniversary of Pontypridd bridge, the coastal path in Anglesey opens, and Chepstow racecourse hosts its first National Motor show. Thieves steal the Cardiff Castle clock hands, while Swansea debuts the new Eisteddfod pink tent. The Queen opens the new Assembly building, and Katherine Jenkins sings at Llangollen. Plus a world record attempt for the largest gathering of Joneses in one place.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents this high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team featuring rugby player and podcaster Joe Marler, actor Jennie McAlpine, comedian Geoff Norcott and presenter Jean Johannson as they take on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Anna Haugh’s Big Irish Food Tour
programme.desc: Comedian Katherine Ryan takes Anna to the foodie capital of Ireland. Will this change Katherine's mind?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Briony May Williams is property-shopping in rural Herefordshire, helping an excited couple who are looking to buy their very first home together where they can finally get their enormous collection of potted plants in the ground. Briony also meets another couple who developed a natural cider business after they made their dream country escape in search of a more self-sufficient lifestyle.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: They say don't walk under a ladder... Jacqui does more than that, and designer Ayo unlocks the potential of a £2 table with a bold design.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Helen and Kevin are nearing full retirement and have a garden dominated by three things – a patio that looks too big for the space, a breeze-block wall that looks ugly and a shed that sticks out like a sore thumb. Inspired by Portugal's granite stone sets and raised boardwalks, they like the idea of a low-maintenance seaside garden with little or no lawn and drought-resistant plants like thistles and grasses. With a budget of £4,000, Charlie and Lee have a challenge ahead to craft this coastal oasis despite being 100 miles from the sea.

programme.title: Shrek
programme.desc: Animated comedy. In a land of living fairy tales and nursery rhymes, grumpy ogre Shrek, along with the loudmouthed Donkey, joins beautiful but wilful Princess Fiona in tackling Lord Farquaad's evil schemes to exile the exotic from his lands and wed the unwilling princess.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents this high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team featuring rugby player and podcaster Joe Marler, actor Jennie McAlpine, comedian Geoff Norcott and presenter Jean Johannson as they take on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Anna Haugh’s Big Irish Food Tour
programme.desc: Comedian Katherine Ryan takes Anna to the foodie capital of Ireland. Katherine’s memories of her grandmother’s over-boiled and under-seasoned meals have left her with a bad impression of Irish food, but Anna is on a mission to change that. First stop is the world-renowned Ballymaloe Cookery School, somewhere that inspired Anna's own culinary journey, followed by a visit to one of the oldest food markets in Europe, the English Market. Will this change Katherine's mind?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer

Natasha visits the International Bomber Command Centre in Lincoln to learn of an Allied mission to save nearly one million Dutch lives.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Briony May Williams is property-shopping in rural Herefordshire, helping an excited couple who are looking to buy their very first home together where they can finally get their enormous collection of potted plants in the ground. They are delighted by the property options presented to them, and a surprise phone call at the end of the search has everyone holding their breath! Briony also meets another couple who developed a natural cider business after they made their dream country escape in search of a more self-sufficient lifestyle.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: They say don't walk under a ladder... Jacqui does more than that, and designer Ayo unlocks the potential of a £2 table with a bold design.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Helen and Kevin are nearing full retirement and have a garden dominated by three things – a patio that looks too big for the space, a breeze-block wall that looks ugly and a shed that sticks out like a sore thumb. Inspired by Portugal's granite stone sets and raised boardwalks, they like the idea of a low-maintenance seaside garden with little or no lawn and drought-resistant plants like thistles and grasses. With a budget of £4,000, Charlie and Lee have a challenge ahead to craft this coastal oasis despite being 100 miles from the sea.

programme.title: Shrek
programme.desc: Animated comedy. In a land of living fairy tales and nursery rhymes, grumpy ogre Shrek, along with the loudmouthed Donkey, joins beautiful but wilful Princess Fiona in tackling Lord Farquaad's evil schemes to exile the exotic from his lands and wed the unwilling princess.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents this high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team featuring rugby player and podcaster Joe Marler, actor Jennie McAlpine, comedian Geoff Norcott and presenter Jean Johannson as they take on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

But it sets off a chain of events that will change them all forever. Zoe begins to wonder if there are bigger forces at play. We are in Greece, after all, land of the gods.

programme.title: Two Weeks in August

programme.title: Reporting Scotland
programme.desc: All the weekend national, UK-wide and international news on Saturday evening at 7.

programme.title: Sportscene: Scottish Cup
programme.desc: Dougie Donnelly presents highlights from the Scottish Cup final as Celtic take on Dunfermline at Hampden Park. Pars manager Neil Lennon, formerly both manager and player at Celtic, will be looking to bring the cup back to Dunfermline for the first time since 1968. Martin O’Neill’s Celtic, however, have won the trophy twice in the last three years and will look to make up for last year’s final defeat to Aberdeen. We bring you the best of the action, plus post-match analysis, interviews and reaction from a huge Saturday in the Scottish football calendar.

programme.title: Icons of Football
programme.desc: Davie Cooper holds a unique place in Scottish football folklore. This portrait of the Rangers and Motherwell legend picks apart the many sides to one of the greatest and often misunderstood players of his generation. Bestowed with a talent and a left foot that could have taken him anywhere in his career, Davie refused overtures to leave out of a deep-rooted attachment to his family and his Lanarkshire upbringing. Despite his unrivalled talent, Davie suffered setbacks, but he always rose to the challenge and delivered. With contributions from Graeme Souness, Derek Ferguson, Iain Ferguson, and the unique insights of his brother John.

programme.title: Scotland's Home of the Year
programme.desc: The judges have travelled the country in their search for Scotland’s home of the year 2026. Now the six regional winners go head-to-head for the title.

programme.title: Only Child
programme.desc: Ken needs to resit his driving exam in order to win back his licence. Richard offers to take him out on a mock test, not realising just how rusty his dad has become behind the wheel.

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: An oddball family make a brave, but bungling, attempt to save their failing funeral home in the sleepy Scottish fishing village of Kincully. Archie, having recently inherited the floundering family business from his domineering dad, is determined to prove himself. His sister Moira, the company mortician, and hearse driver Cousin Ron are looking to Archie to prevent A Better Place Funeral Home from falling into the hands of Sympathy Plus, a corporate funeral chain run by the power-hungry Eileen. Archie is also living in the shadow of his late father - literally. He keeps him in a great big freezer on the landing. With time running out, Archie hatches a plan to keep hold of the family business. Will Archie’s scheme work? Or will A Better Place fall prey to Eileen’s growing empire?

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Calamity James is a slapstick comedy about a young man, James, who is cursed with ‘acute misfortune syndrome’. James tries to reconnect with his dad after being thrown out by his mum for setting fire to their house at a family barbecue. In this world, chronic bad luck exists and the unbelievable is the everyday.

programme.title: Highland Cops
programme.desc: PC Cailean McLeod returns to his home island of Lewis to search for a missing 16-year-old who walked out into the snow and has now been missing for 48 hours. In the stunning landscape of Glencoe, police have to deal with traffic chaos while trying to free a motorhome from a roadside ditch. In Shetland, it’s the busiest night of the year as police deal with Viking revellers and a drunk driver.

programme.title: Mark Walters in the Footsteps of Andrew Watson
programme.desc: Former Rangers player Mark Walters looks back at his career with the Glasgow club to assess the racism he faced while playing for them. Watching harrowing footage of his early matches, he vividly describes the visceral atmosphere as he was targeted by opposition fans. In a candid conversation with Graeme Souness, the player-manager who brought him to Ibrox, Mark reveals the inner resilience that got him through those tough games and reflects on how unconscious bias in TV commentary affects the way black footballers are perceived today. Mark also finds out about early black footballing pioneers in Scotland, including an early multiracial football team who played a stone's throw from Ibrox stadium. He unearths the incredible story of Andrew Watson, the world’s first black international player, who captained the Scotland national team in 1881 to its greatest ever win over England. Watson was a complex figure who was both the descendant of slaves and the beneficiary of slavery. Mark asks how Andrew overcame racism to be welcomed into the footballing elite in the 1880s.

programme.title: Big Proud Party Agency
programme.desc: Best friends Lauren and Tamara from Cheshire are keen to mark the difficult journey of their friend Miya, who underwent gender confirmation surgery a few years ago and has now blossomed into the person she always wanted to be. By celebrating her ‘V Day’, they want to show her how special she is and how much she means to them. After hearing Miya’s incredible story, the party agents compete to win the business. Ryan wants to host a rooftop reception that celebrates transgender visibility. Teddy hopes her three-parties-in-one pitch gets her the gig and Christopher is inspired by butterflies with his 'woodland wilderness' themed event. After Lauren and Tamara choose their favourite party idea, it’s time to get down to business. The winning party agent, supported by the others, heads off to put their plan into action. There are photoshoots to plan, venues to be dressed and red carpets to be rolled out. Will Miya have a ‘V-Day’ to remember?

programme.title: Big Proud Party Agency
programme.desc: Best friends Ryan and Daniel from Belfast want to throw the mother of all comeback shows for their friend and fellow wrestler Shannon. Shannon - aka Skye James, the Rainbow Rebel - injured herself badly performing her signature move nearly two years ago and hasn’t stepped into a ring since. The boys are hoping the Big Proud Party Agency can step up and help her get back through the ropes. After hearing what’s at stake, the party agents compete to win the business. Ryan unveils his 80s arcade-inspired, neon-drenched wrestling smackdown. Teddy campaigns for a rebellion-themed street party, and Christopher wants to create the ultimate fight club in an underground car park. After Ryan and Daniel choose their favourite party idea, it’s time to get down to business. The winning party agent, supported by the others, heads to Belfast to put their plan into action. They need to find a party venue that can accommodate a wrestling ring, design the perfect fighting outfit and taste-test a signature cocktail that will hopefully toast a comeback victory!

Wesley comes back to Runcorn in an attempt to win back Donna's heart and asks Gaz for advice on what to do. Gaz advises Wesley that he needs to be more like him.

programme.title: Women's Super League
programme.desc: Coverage of the Women's Super League play-off as Charlton Athletic face Leicester City.

programme.title: Great Bear Stakeout
programme.desc: In this episode, the world-famous salmon run arrives in Alaska. The bears must catch hundreds of these fish if they are to bulk up and survive the harsh winter months. We discover that young grizzly mum Parsnip and her cub Pushki have returned to the bay to feed on the salmon. But predatory adult bears will kill cubs and, with fierce competition, Parsnip must protect her cub and learn the skills of fishing if they are to both make it through hibernation. As winter approaches, life gets more intense, survival gets tougher, and the threats get even greater.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from the National Maritime Museum Cornwall, based in Falmouth. The museum explores the region's seafaring history and hosts our antiques experts Charles Hanson and Caroline Hawley. Turning up out of the hundreds of bags and boxes are a model yacht and a Newlyn copper tray. And presenter Paul Martin investigates the work of controversial local artist Henry Scott Tuke.

programme.title: UEFA Women's Champions League
programme.desc: All the action from the Women's Champions League final as Barcelona play Lyon in Oslo.

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Lochs
programme.desc: Paul’s loch-hopping journey starts on the west coast on a wild and windswept stretch of Loch Hourn. Travelling inland, Paul reaches sheltered Loch Quoich, where he hears tales of Scotland’s last outlaw. On the shores of Loch Lochy, he meets a couple who had a memorable encounter with a monster from the deep called Lizzie. A detour south leads to a ruined bridge where the first shots were fired of the ’45. Paul then walks an old railway line above the Great Glen and inhales diesel smoke from a reeking shunter at a station undergoing restoration. A canal journey takes him to Fort Augustus, where he searches for the original fort. On Loch Ness, Paul meets a man who, when still a schoolboy, met the fastest man on water, John Cobb aka the Gentle Giant.

programme.title: RHS Chelsea Flower Show
programme.desc: Monty Don and Rachel de Thame look back at the highlights of their week at the RHS Chelsea Flower Show 2026. They celebrate some of this year’s inspirational garden designs and the horticultural excellence on display in the Great Pavilion. Also, they share the latest planting ideas and design trends that have been revealed this year.

programme.title: Cher at the BBC
programme.desc: Turn back time on a journey through the BBC archives to celebrate singing superstar Cher and her 75th birthday. This selection of songs and chat show moments features many of the hits that have made Cher the only artist to have US number ones in each of the past six decades. Including favourites like Believe, Love and Understanding, Walking in Memphis and her first UK chart topper I Got You Babe, recorded with ex-husband and singing partner Sonny Bono.

programme.title: Cher Meets Rylan
programme.desc: The goddess of pop sits down for a fun and in-depth chat with Rylan Clark about her new record, biggest hits, and incredible life and career. Featuring archive footage from across the decades of Cher's hit records and television appearances, illustrating her glittering music career, success in film, iconic fashion choices and the ways she has influenced so many people.

programme.title: My Week with Marilyn
programme.desc: It is 1956, and The Prince and the Showgirl is being made at Pinewood Studios in London, directed by and starring Laurence Olivier, who has recruited one of the biggest Hollywood stars of all time, Marilyn Monroe, to co-star with him. Colin Clark, a junior assistant on the production, is assigned the job of looking after Marilyn and keeps a journal about the week he spent with her. It proves to be a turbulent experience as Marilyn is going through marital problems with her husband and uses Colin as a much-needed sounding board for all her pent-up neurosis. Acclaimed drama from BBC Films based on Clark's real-life diaries.

The What’s in the Box? game reveals a superhero mask, and when the toddlers and parents open up a bigger box, they discover lots more objects and toys that are inspired by superheroes. Storytime is all about joining in with physical actions, as Benjee Bear and Bailee Bear visit the park to practise their superhero skills! Viewers at home show how they’ve been exploring the superheroes theme too. And, The Circle Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with stretching and the Goodbye song.

But will Nana enjoy the cakes? And will the worm be alright?

Storytime is all about joining in with physical actions, as Benjee Bear and Bailee Bear visit the park to practise their superhero skills! Viewers at home show how they’ve been exploring the superheroes theme too. And, The Circle Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with stretching and the Goodbye song.

programme.title: What’s in Your Plant Pot?
programme.desc: Chilli farmer Amrit Madhoo and the Fact Pack explore the colourful world of chillies. They discover how they grow, how ladybirds help protect the plants, and why not all chillies are spicy.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Kyra and Khloe plan a visit to Nana and make chocolate crispy cakes to surprise her with. Visiting Nana is a special occasion, so Mum draws pretty patterns on Kyra and Khloe’s hands using henna. At Nana’s they have a delicious picnic in the garden and then rescue a worm! But will Nana enjoy the cakes? And will the worm be alright?

programme.title: Stan Can
programme.desc: Butterflies on Stanley's solar panels mean he has no power for his vehicles or his Can-Bots! Luckily, Seamus and Little Woo know a thing or two about butterflies. Stanley creates a giant flower to lead them to a new home.

programme.title: The Game Catchers
programme.desc: The Game Catchers land on the Pixel Art Planet, where they learn to play water, flame, fire. But the game is interrupted after a Pipikini pecks at a rainbow, causing a shower of pixels!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: It’s a slow day in the big city, until disaster strikes. Numberblock Three has lost one of her red juggling ball buttons! Can detective Numberblock One help Three solve this mysterious case by telling the time? Will Three ever juggle again? It’s a sticky situation, but only time will tell if One can find out where the missing ball is and close the case.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Red and Blue meet Yellow and have fun colouring the seaside. Discover the colours around you.

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: A dusty, old box on the top of the wardrobe is causing sneezing and mayhem. What’s inside? Rebecca and Murphi make a monster from a tissue box, and the Mini Monsters create their own monster glove puppets. Uncle Ernie calls to tell Rebecca about his rare bird photography but is distracted by falling coconuts. Finally, an old sock becomes a fabulous flamingo puppet, with some assistance from the Tiny Helpers.

programme.title: Talking Tom Heroes: Suddenly Super
programme.desc: Gor-don the Great steals Angela’s superspeed.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers make pictures from leaf rubbings. They visit different trees in the garden and learn why each of them is important to wildlife in the area.

programme.title: Andy's Dino Island
programme.desc: Andy and Jen are throwing themselves a party to celebrate an epic year on Dino Island but discover that their prehistoric pals have been helping themselves to all the party food.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Snake tells Slug to hurry up and join him for a new Squirrel Club adventure, Norrie counts shells on a beach, then it's time for a game! Finally, learn a skipping song with the Squirrels. Eugene teaches everyone how to create a song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: In Tall Trees Forest, Lisa and the children have bubbly fun washing toy clothes, learning British Sign Language signs for jungle, clothes and washing, then they sing and sign Down in the Jungle.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger teaches the baby Pea-Rexes a new survival skill through a game of hide-and-seek.

programme.title: Nick Cope's Popcast
programme.desc: Nick is trying his best to bake a special cake for Grandma’s birthday, but things don’t go to plan. The Popcasters tell him to keep on trying and he’ll get there in the end.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Koa’s cone makes him feel special, so he asks Vida for one more day to wear it. But the cone gets in the way of everything! Can Vida help Koa find another way to feel special?

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: Zog cures Fifi’s hiccups with a big dragon roar. But when patients are too scared to be treated by him, Zog must choose between being a scary dragon or a doctor.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi and Aunty T visit the Manchester Museum. Rafi thinks dinosaurs are more than fine and wishes for a real one. Suddenly, Slurpy the triceratops appears! Slurpy is cheeky - he slurps faces, leaves colourful footprints and knocks things over while munching salad. Rafi worries about the mess, but Aunty T laughs and enjoys the fun. When the wish ends, Slurpy disappears, and Aunty T uses her own wand to put the museum back together. She admits dinosaurs and museums are magic, and Rafi beams with delight.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey discovers that mothering is much harder than she imagined!

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo wants to go somewhere new, so Gran Gran takes her to discover new places in the local community. They visit Jared's shop, the community garden and the roof of the library, spotting lots of new things along the way. JoJo realises that even when you think you know somewhere, there are always new places to discover.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah decides that octagons are her favourite shape and starts an eight-person club to celebrate!

programme.title: Charlie and Lola
programme.desc: Children's animation. Charlie loves his little sister Lola, even if at times she can be infuriating. Charlie and Lola are looking forward to seeing a Chinese puppet show, but they are in a squabbling mood. In fact, they are doing nothing but squabbling. Will they ever simmer down and learn how to talk nicely to each other?

programme.title: Moon and Me
programme.desc: Inside the little Toy House, each of the friends decides to give Lily Plant some 'pretend water'. Everybody loves Lily Plant. Lily Plant loves pretend water. What a lovely day for Lily Plant!

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa create a leaf picture, but the wind blows the leaves away. At Play Time, they decorate a pot - but it breaks when BaBa accidentally drops it. At Yummy Time, they decorate a special cookie and bring it with them across the Lullaby Lake. They have been trying to make a gift for Gramma Leeba, who reassures them that the best gift is made with love.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: In a magical forest, colourful characters have adventures. Igglepiggle and Upsy Daisy join the Tombliboos for a ride on the Pinky Ponk.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: Rusty squeaks. None of the other robots on Planet Robotone squeak and this makes him sad. But with the help of his robot friends, Rusty learns that it's good to be different. Actress Sharon D Clarke makes this sci-fi story sing!

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: On the rugged shores of Ballintoy, famed as the Iron Islands in Game of Thrones, Dermot journeys into the Atlantic with local fisherman Gordy, in search of the thrill of the catch along one of Ireland's most dramatic coastlines. Back ashore, Gordy and Dermot transport Dermot back to his childhood, cooking up their catch. Dermot travels to Bushmills, and steps into the kitchen of acclaimed restaurant Tartine. Joining chef Gary Stewart, Dermot cooks up a local favourite dessert: whiskey-infused rhubarb and custard. In search of more fine Irish whiskey, Dermot visits the Giant's Causeway, where, perched on ancient stones above crashing waves, he joins a legendary storyteller and whiskey expert for an unforgettable experience.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: On the sweeping sands of Benone Strand, Dermot rolls up his trousers and wades into the sea to harvest water for salt-making. Guided by Clare from Mussenden Salt, he learns the traditional process of creating sea salt over an open fire right on the beach. Embracing ancient Irish traditions, they host a clan-style cookout, roasting meat, cheese, and vegetables over open flames as previous generations once did. Travelling on to Coleraine, Dermot joins local lobster fisherman Peter, heading out onto the water to haul in pots. With fresh lobster secured, Dermot visits LIR Seafood Restaurant, where husband-and-wife team Rebekah and Stevie champion a zero-waste approach to cooking. In the kitchen, Dermot gets hands-on, learning to prepare indulgent lobster rolls while discovering how thoughtful cooking can turn every part of the catch into something delicious.

programme.title: Nobody's Fool
programme.desc: Emily Atack and Danny Dyer host a strategic reality quiz packed full of drama and deception. A group of ten strangers arrive at Danny and Emily’s manor to compete for up to £100 000 in a brand new game where survival depends on not just how smart you are, but how smart others think you are.. From the moment they arrive, the players are thrown straight into brain teasing challenges, keeping them occupied outside the gate. The first private pod quiz introduces the show’s central tension: money is earned in secret, then publicly declared and the players must eliminate the person who they believe has contributed the least to the prize pot. Exaggeration, denial and bluffing creep in fast, leaving the group unsure who to trust. When the house must vote for the worst performing player, personal grudges and first impressions start to outway evidence - and with half the prize pot at stake for ejecting the wrong player, the stakes couldn't be higher.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: On the sweeping sands of Benone Strand, Dermot rolls up his trousers and wades into the sea to harvest water for salt-making. Guided by Clare from Mussenden Salt, he learns the traditional process of creating sea salt over an open fire right on the beach. Embracing ancient Irish traditions, they host a clan-style cookout, roasting meat, cheese, and vegetables over open flames as previous generations once did. Travelling on to Coleraine, Dermot joins local lobster fisherman Peter, heading out onto the water to haul in pots. With fresh lobster secured, Dermot visits LIR Seafood Restaurant, where husband-and-wife team Rebekah and Stevie champion a zero-waste approach to cooking. In the kitchen, Dermot gets hands-on, learning to prepare indulgent lobster rolls while discovering how thoughtful cooking can turn every part of the catch into something delicious.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: On the sweeping sands of Benone Strand, Dermot rolls up his trousers and wades into the sea to harvest water for salt-making. Guided by Clare from Mussenden Salt, he learns the traditional process of creating sea salt over an open fire right on the beach. Embracing ancient Irish traditions, they host a clan-style cookout, roasting meat, cheese, and vegetables over open flames as previous generations once did. Travelling on to Coleraine, Dermot joins local lobster fisherman Peter, heading out onto the water to haul in pots. With fresh lobster secured, Dermot visits LIR Seafood Restaurant, where husband-and-wife team Rebekah and Stevie champion a zero-waste approach to cooking. In the kitchen, Dermot gets hands-on, learning to prepare indulgent lobster rolls while discovering how thoughtful cooking can turn every part of the catch into something delicious.

programme.title: Nobody's Fool
programme.desc: Emily Atack and Danny Dyer host a strategic reality quiz packed full of drama and deception. A group of ten strangers arrive at Danny and Emily’s manor to compete for up to £100 000 in a brand new game where survival depends on not just how smart you are, but how smart others think you are.. From the moment they arrive, the players are thrown straight into brain teasing challenges, keeping them occupied outside the gate. The first private pod quiz introduces the show’s central tension: money is earned in secret, then publicly declared and the players must eliminate the person who they believe has contributed the least to the prize pot. Exaggeration, denial and bluffing creep in fast, leaving the group unsure who to trust. When the house must vote for the worst performing player, personal grudges and first impressions start to outway evidence - and with half the prize pot at stake for ejecting the wrong player, the stakes couldn't be higher.

programme.title: Nobody's Fool
programme.desc: Emily Atack and Danny Dyer host a strategic reality quiz packed full of drama and deception. A group of ten strangers arrive at Danny and Emily’s manor to compete for up to £100 000 in a brand new game where survival depends on not just how smart you are, but how smart others think you are.. From the moment they arrive, the players are thrown straight into brain teasing challenges, keeping them occupied outside the gate. The first private pod quiz introduces the show’s central tension: money is earned in secret, then publicly declared and the players must eliminate the person who they believe has contributed the least to the prize pot. Exaggeration, denial and bluffing creep in fast, leaving the group unsure who to trust. When the house must vote for the worst performing player, personal grudges and first impressions start to outway evidence - and with half the prize pot at stake for ejecting the wrong player, the stakes couldn't be higher.

programme.title: Nobody's Fool
programme.desc: Emily Atack and Danny Dyer host a strategic reality quiz packed full of drama and deception. A group of ten strangers arrive at Danny and Emily’s manor to compete for up to £100 000 in a brand new game where survival depends on not just how smart you are, but how smart others think you are.. From the moment they arrive, the players are thrown straight into brain teasing challenges, keeping them occupied outside the gate. The first private pod quiz introduces the show’s central tension: money is earned in secret, then publicly declared and the players must eliminate the person who they believe has contributed the least to the prize pot. Exaggeration, denial and bluffing creep in fast, leaving the group unsure who to trust. When the house must vote for the worst performing player, personal grudges and first impressions start to outway evidence - and with half the prize pot at stake for ejecting the wrong player, the stakes couldn't be higher.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: On the rugged shores of Ballintoy, famed as the Iron Islands in Game of Thrones, Dermot journeys into the Atlantic with local fisherman Gordy, in search of the thrill of the catch along one of Ireland's most dramatic coastlines. Back ashore, Gordy and Dermot transport Dermot back to his childhood, cooking up their catch. Dermot travels to Bushmills, and steps into the kitchen of acclaimed restaurant Tartine. Joining chef Gary Stewart, Dermot cooks up a local favourite dessert: whiskey-infused rhubarb and custard. In search of more fine Irish whiskey, Dermot visits the Giant's Causeway, where, perched on ancient stones above crashing waves, he joins a legendary storyteller and whiskey expert for an unforgettable experience.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: On the sweeping sands of Benone Strand, Dermot rolls up his trousers and wades into the sea to harvest water for salt-making. Guided by Clare from Mussenden Salt, he learns the traditional process of creating sea salt over an open fire right on the beach. Embracing ancient Irish traditions, they host a clan-style cookout, roasting meat, cheese, and vegetables over open flames as previous generations once did. Travelling on to Coleraine, Dermot joins local lobster fisherman Peter, heading out onto the water to haul in pots. With fresh lobster secured, Dermot visits LIR Seafood Restaurant, where husband-and-wife team Rebekah and Stevie champion a zero-waste approach to cooking. In the kitchen, Dermot gets hands-on, learning to prepare indulgent lobster rolls while discovering how thoughtful cooking can turn every part of the catch into something delicious.

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: After Garfield slightly changes the recipe of Odie's birthday cake, it comes to life and spreads panic in town!

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Garfield has been mean to Odie again. Left in the garden, he's taken in by a neighbour, Nathan. Odie is happy with this new friendship, but he soon discovers that Garfield wasn't that bad after all...

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Garfield takes us through the ages to tell us the history of dogs. As we know, he has a poor opinion of them, but an incident will make him change his mind. After all, all dogs are not useless!

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Garfield is bored. He has nothing to do. Well, not exactly: watching Odie and the squirrels in the garden, there's fun ahead after all!

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Eddie Gourmand has built a super attraction park, made completely out of cheese. Squeak and his friends beg Garfield to take them there but with Harry working as a security guard, it won't be easy!

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Pooky has disappeared again, but this time, it's Nermal who finds it. He is willing to give it back to him at one condition: Garfield has to be really nice to Nermal for the rest of the day!

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Garfield's cat instincts push him to climb on a tree. But how will he get down? Everyone tries to give him a hand, but they end up stuck in that tree! Now he's out on a limb; who will save him?

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Nermal doesn't believe in super heroes. Garfield does and he tries desperately to convince him. Even if that means disguising himself as Ultra Powerful Guy.

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Garfield receives a strange helmet which lets him read everyone's thoughts. He even catches aliens' conversations who are just about to conquer Earth! Garfield has to stop this plot immediately!

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: After Odie dreams of being a super hero, Garfield mocks him for it. But when Garfield really gets into trouble, Odie puts his grudges aside and flies off to help him. And this time he REALLY flies!

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Nermal makes a bet with Garfield: if Garfield manages not to eat for a whole hour, he won't see Nermal for a whole month. Will Garfield be victorious ?

programme.title: The Garfield Show

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: On the rugged shores of Ballintoy, famed as the Iron Islands in Game of Thrones, Dermot journeys into the Atlantic with local fisherman Gordy, in search of the thrill of the catch along one of Ireland's most dramatic coastlines. Back ashore, Gordy and Dermot transport Dermot back to his childhood, cooking up their catch. Dermot travels to Bushmills, and steps into the kitchen of acclaimed restaurant Tartine. Joining chef Gary Stewart, Dermot cooks up a local favourite dessert: whiskey-infused rhubarb and custard. In search of more fine Irish whiskey, Dermot visits the Giant's Causeway, where, perched on ancient stones above crashing waves, he joins a legendary storyteller and whiskey expert for an unforgettable experience.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: On the sweeping sands of Benone Strand, Dermot rolls up his trousers and wades into the sea to harvest water for salt-making. Guided by Clare from Mussenden Salt, he learns the traditional process of creating sea salt over an open fire right on the beach. Embracing ancient Irish traditions, they host a clan-style cookout, roasting meat, cheese, and vegetables over open flames as previous generations once did. Travelling on to Coleraine, Dermot joins local lobster fisherman Peter, heading out onto the water to haul in pots. With fresh lobster secured, Dermot visits LIR Seafood Restaurant, where husband-and-wife team Rebekah and Stevie champion a zero-waste approach to cooking. In the kitchen, Dermot gets hands-on, learning to prepare indulgent lobster rolls while discovering how thoughtful cooking can turn every part of the catch into something delicious.

programme.title: Nobody's Fool
programme.desc: Emily Atack and Danny Dyer host a strategic reality quiz packed full of drama and deception. A group of ten strangers arrive at Danny and Emily’s manor to compete for up to £100 000 in a brand new game where survival depends on not just how smart you are, but how smart others think you are.. From the moment they arrive, the players are thrown straight into brain teasing challenges, keeping them occupied outside the gate. The first private pod quiz introduces the show’s central tension: money is earned in secret, then publicly declared and the players must eliminate the person who they believe has contributed the least to the prize pot. Exaggeration, denial and bluffing creep in fast, leaving the group unsure who to trust. When the house must vote for the worst performing player, personal grudges and first impressions start to outway evidence - and with half the prize pot at stake for ejecting the wrong player, the stakes couldn't be higher.

Reawakening after nearly 5,000 years of captivity, Black Adam becomes the world's ruthless protector and an anti-villain to take on the likes of Superman and Wonder Woman - now in the 21st century, Black Adam must face off against the Justice Society of America and heroes including Doctor Fate, Hawkman, Atom Smasher and Cyclone as the fate of the world hangs in the balance.

programme.title: Nobody's Fool
programme.desc: Emily Atack and Danny Dyer host a strategic reality quiz packed full of drama and deception. A group of ten strangers arrive at Danny and Emily’s manor to compete for up to £100 000 in a brand new game where survival depends on not just how smart you are, but how smart others think you are.. From the moment they arrive, the players are thrown straight into brain teasing challenges, keeping them occupied outside the gate. The first private pod quiz introduces the show’s central tension: money is earned in secret, then publicly declared and the players must eliminate the person who they believe has contributed the least to the prize pot. Exaggeration, denial and bluffing creep in fast, leaving the group unsure who to trust. When the house must vote for the worst performing player, personal grudges and first impressions start to outway evidence - and with half the prize pot at stake for ejecting the wrong player, the stakes couldn't be higher.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: On the rugged shores of Ballintoy, famed as the Iron Islands in Game of Thrones, Dermot journeys into the Atlantic with local fisherman Gordy, in search of the thrill of the catch along one of Ireland's most dramatic coastlines. Back ashore, Gordy and Dermot transport Dermot back to his childhood, cooking up their catch. Dermot travels to Bushmills, and steps into the kitchen of acclaimed restaurant Tartine. Joining chef Gary Stewart, Dermot cooks up a local favourite dessert: whiskey-infused rhubarb and custard. In search of more fine Irish whiskey, Dermot visits the Giant's Causeway, where, perched on ancient stones above crashing waves, he joins a legendary storyteller and whiskey expert for an unforgettable experience.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: On the sweeping sands of Benone Strand, Dermot rolls up his trousers and wades into the sea to harvest water for salt-making. Guided by Clare from Mussenden Salt, he learns the traditional process of creating sea salt over an open fire right on the beach. Embracing ancient Irish traditions, they host a clan-style cookout, roasting meat, cheese, and vegetables over open flames as previous generations once did. Travelling on to Coleraine, Dermot joins local lobster fisherman Peter, heading out onto the water to haul in pots. With fresh lobster secured, Dermot visits LIR Seafood Restaurant, where husband-and-wife team Rebekah and Stevie champion a zero-waste approach to cooking. In the kitchen, Dermot gets hands-on, learning to prepare indulgent lobster rolls while discovering how thoughtful cooking can turn every part of the catch into something delicious.
